# Ancient Engineering Technologies

> > UW–Madison educational resource exploring ancient water management, construction materials, and engineering innovations from civilizations including Egypt, Greece, Rome, Teotihuacan, Machu Picchu, Venice, and the Netherlands.

This site, maintained by the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering at UW–Madison, presents student research on ancient engineering technologies with emphasis on water systems, construction techniques, and sustainable practices. The collection highlights how ancient civilizations solved complex engineering challenges through innovations in hydraulics, materials science, and urban planning.

## Key Topics

- Ancient water management and purification
- Roman concrete and construction materials
- Greek engineering and Minoan water systems
- Egyptian Nile engineering and irrigation
- Pompeii aqueducts and sanitation
- Venice lagoon engineering and wooden piles
- Teotihuacan pyramid construction
- Machu Picchu Incan terraces
- Dutch windmills and polder drainage
- Mediterranean engineering traditions
- Ancient urban planning and infrastructure
- Sustainable engineering practices
- Historical hydraulic systems

## Overview

- [Ancient Engineering Technologies](https://ancientengrtech.wisc.edu): UW-Madison site on ancient engineering technologies and student research

## Ancient Civilizations

- [Ancient Greece](https://ancientengrtech.wisc.edu/greece-overview): Minoan civilization water systems and Greek engineering overview
- [Pompeii](https://ancientengrtech.wisc.edu/pompeii): Mount Vesuvius eruption, Roman engineering, and Pompeii preservation
- [Teotihuacan](https://ancientengrtech.wisc.edu/teotihuacan): Mesoamerican city planning and measurement systems in Teotihuacan
- [Machu Picchu](https://ancientengrtech.wisc.edu/machu-picchu): Incan water management and agricultural terraces at Machu Picchu, Peru
- [Venice Overview](https://ancientengrtech.wisc.edu/venice): Venice Venetian Lagoon settlement, pilings, and 5th-century refuge

## Water Management and Hydraulic Systems

- [Ancient Egypt Water Engineering](https://ancientengrtech.wisc.edu/ancient-egypt-water-engineering): Ancient Egyptian water purification, irrigation, and Nile engineering methods
- [Ancient Egypt Water Technologies](https://ancientengrtech.wisc.edu/ancient-egypt-water-technologies): Egyptian coagulation and Nile River water purification techniques
- [Greek Water Systems](https://ancientengrtech.wisc.edu/greece-overview/water-systems): Minoan clay pipes, Knossos sewage, and Athens plumbing systems
- [Greek Water Quality](https://ancientengrtech.wisc.edu/greece-overview/water-quality): Alcmaeon of Croton's water quality assessments in ancient Greece
- [Pompeii Water Distribution](https://ancientengrtech.wisc.edu/pompeii/water-distribution): Pompeii aqueduct systems, public fountains, and Roman water distribution
- [Pompeii Water Collection](https://ancientengrtech.wisc.edu/pompeii/water-collection): Castellum Aquae and Augustan aqueduct water collection in Pompeii
- [Pompeii Sanitation](https://ancientengrtech.wisc.edu/pompeii/sanitation): Roman toilets, street drainage, and wastewater systems in Pompeii
- [Venice Water Management](https://ancientengrtech.wisc.edu/venice/venice-content): Venice lagoon engineering, wooden piles, and acqua alta management

## Construction Materials and Techniques

- [Roman Concrete](https://ancientengrtech.wisc.edu/roman-concrete): Roman concrete composition, pozzolana use, and durability techniques
- [Teotihuacan Construction](https://ancientengrtech.wisc.edu/teotihuacan/construction): Teotihuacan pyramid construction using basalt, tezontle, and andesite
- [Teotihuacan Pyramids](https://ancientengrtech.wisc.edu/teotihuacan/pyramids): Pyramid of the Moon and Sun construction along Avenue of the Dead

## Wind Power and Mechanical Engineering

- [The Netherlands Windmill](https://ancientengrtech.wisc.edu/the-netherlands-windmill): Dutch windmill types, grain milling, and drainage system history
- [Windmill History and Development](https://ancientengrtech.wisc.edu/the-netherlands-windmill-history-and-why-to-build): Dutch windmill development for flood control and polder drainage
- [Sustainable Wind Power](https://ancientengrtech.wisc.edu/sustainable-wind-power): Wind turbine types, mechanics, and renewable energy generation
